column5: Intro
column6: Objective
column7: Outro

column5: You washed up breathing, which is more than the rest of the crew managed. Get on your feet and find the market before the tide turns.
column6: Find the market stall in the camp.
column7: Good. A captain who can walk can still give orders.

column5: Two cutthroats are picking over the wreck like gulls. Put them down and the camp eats tonight.
column6: Kill 2 cutthroats.
column7: Blooded. The crew felt that one.

column5: Old Bell buried a stash by the tents before the storm. Crack it open, the coin is yours.
column6: Open the camp chest.
column7: Coin in hand and the day barely started.

column5: A navy patrol is sniffing along the ridge. Three cadets, three graves, and the cove stays ours.
column6: Kill 3 navy cadets.
column7: The ridge is quiet again. Let the navy wonder why.

column5: Every free pirate works the bounty board. Take the cutthroat bounty and come back paid.
column6: Turn in the Cutthroat Bounty at the board.
column7: Now you know where the coin lives.

column5: There is a boat moored at the pier with nobody at the tiller. Take her out and remind the sea who you are.
column6: Walk onto the pier beside the small boat and press F to board.
column7: You have a deck under you again, Captain.

column5: The bone captain holds the old fort and no crew will follow you while he stands. End him.
column6: Kill the Skeleton Captain at the fort.
column7: The cove is yours, Captain. Now go see Jerold the blacksmith. A captain needs steel that bites, and the rest of this island will not know your name until he says it.

column5: Jerold works the bench past the market. Tell him the cove has a captain again and he will find you an edge.
column6: Speak to Jerold the blacksmith at the smithy.
column7: Jerold looks you over and grunts. From him that is a welcome.

column5: Steel that never sees my bench is just a heavy stick. Buy one tier off me and feel the difference.
column6: Buy any upgrade tier at the smithy.
column7: Now it bites. Come back when you want it to bite harder.

column5: Bone grinds sharper than any stone I own. Bring me four deckhands worth of it.
column6: Kill 4 skeleton deckhands.
column7: Four sacks of grit. My wheel will sing for a month.

column5: There is good iron in the wreck chest on the far shore and I am too old to swim for it.
column6: Open the wreck chest on the far shore.
column7: Salt eaten but sound. This will make somebody a cutlass.

column5: Marta runs her tavern out of a tent by the smugglers' stash, east past the tents. She has been asking after a pair of pot hooks. Go take her order for me.
column6: Find Marta at the stash camp east of the tents.
column7: Marta wipes her hands and looks you over. So you are the new captain.

column5: Three cutthroats drank my last barrel and paid me in laughter. Settle the bill.
column6: Kill 3 cutthroats.
column7: That is the bill settled. Sit down, the first cup is mine.

column5: My empties went down to the pier and never came back. Go count what is still standing by the boat, then tell me the worst of it.
column6: Check the barrels at the pier beside the boat.
column7: Half of them split. Well, at least I know.

column5: A crew follows the captain who buys. Forty gold and every cup in the room is full.
column6: Pay Marta 40 gold for a round.
column7: Listen to them. That is what loyalty sounds like when you pour it. Cobb keeps the harbour post down at the pier. Go and let him log you.

column5: I keep this pier and I know every hull on it. A captain with a crew needs one under him, so take that boat out past the moorings for me.
column6: Board your boat at the pier.
column7: She holds. Barely, but she holds.

column5: There is a rock out past the shallows that eats hulls. Sail to it, then come back and tell me where it sits.
column6: Sail out to the far rock past the pier.
column7: Sixty fathoms of nothing and one rock. Now the harbour knows.

column5: Bring a bounty in to the board up at the camp and I will log you as a working captain of this harbour.
column6: Turn in any bounty at the camp's bounty board.
column7: Logged and stamped. This harbour knows your name now.

column5: Cutthroats keep drifting in off the sand. Thin them for me and the coin is yours.
column6: Kill 3 cutthroats for Bell.
column7: The sand is quiet again. Come back when it is not.

column5: Take this tally down to Jerold and bring me back what he says.
column6: Carry Bell's tally to Jerold the blacksmith, then report back.
column7: He said what I thought he would say. Here is your cut.

column5: More bone, more grit. Three deckhands and I will pay the going rate.
column6: Kill 3 skeleton deckhands for Jerold.
column7: Good weight. The wheel eats well tonight.

column5: Coal does not walk here on its own. Twenty five gold keeps the bench hot.
column6: Pay Jerold 25 gold for coal.
column7: Hot bench, sharp steel. You will thank me.

column5: They are dry again and looking at me like gulls. Thirty gold and I will pour.
column6: Pay Marta 30 gold for the crew.
column7: Look at them go. Worth every coin.

column5: Cobb wants a count of my empties. Walk it down to the harbour post at the pier before he walks all the way up here for it.
column6: Carry Marta's count down to Cobb at the pier, then report back.
column7: He grumbled, so he read it. That is payment enough for him.

column5: Navy cadets are counting our masts again. Three of them, and the harbour keeps its secrets.
column6: Kill 3 navy cadets for Cobb.
column7: Nothing to report to their captain now. Good.

column5: Somebody has to read the tide off the pier and my knees are done with ladders.
column6: Walk out to your boat at the pier and read the tide.
column7: Two hands under the mark. Written down and paid for.

column5: There is a reach south-east of here the navy hung a captain of mine on. Sail out and put your boots on that sand, then come back and tell me it is still there.
column6: Sail south-east and land on Gallows Reach.
column7: So it stands. Find the sergeant who wears the coat and hates it, and mind the lighthouse.

column5: I keep the muster book and I keep the truth apart from it. Three marines off the square and nobody counts them twice.
column6: Kill 3 navy marines on the square.
column7: Three lines I will not write. Good.

column5: They keep the powder in a shed with one lock and two drunks. The chest under the crates is not on any list.
column6: Open the chest in the powder magazine.
column7: Nothing in there was ever the Crown's. Take it. That rusty flintlock still has a shot left in it.

column5: Climb the lighthouse and stand on the top. Whoever holds that light holds every hull that comes in at night.
column6: Climb to the top of the lighthouse.
column7: You saw the whole reach from up there. So does Harrow.

column5: Harrow gave the order at the gallows. He stands there still, as if the rope were his own work. End him and the reach is nobody's.
column6: Kill Lieutenant Harrow at the gallows.
column7: The reach is quiet. I will burn the muster book tonight.

column5: The square fills up again every watch. Three marines and I will pay you out of the powder money.
column6: Kill 3 navy marines for Ada.
column7: Quiet stones again. Come back when they are not.

column5: Thirty gold buys the shed guard a bottle and a blind eye for a week.
column6: Pay Ada 30 gold for the guard's bottle.
column7: He will not see a thing until Thursday.

column5: The deserters ran to the swamp beyond Wreck Cove. I struck their names from the book. Something worse than the navy took them in. Find Mama Oduya in the stilt village; she remembers who went under.
column6: Land on Mangrove Hollow at the marked beach.
column7: That is the Hollow. Find Oduya above the mud, and keep clear of the bells.

column5: I knew the hands that cast those bells. Now the cult rings them to call more people into the mud. Take three bell keepers off the paths.
column6: Kill 3 bog cultists.
column7: Quiet, for a little while. Now we can hear what lies beneath it.

column5: There is a chest at the stone altar. Its contents belonged to the village before the Mother claimed them. Open it and bring the old promises back into daylight.
column6: Open the Bog Altar Chest.
column7: The village has not forgotten its own. Neither have I.

column5: Her acolytes tie sickness to a living hand. Watch for the green light, and give them no straight path to your heart. Two of them keep the outer watch.
column6: Kill 2 hex acolytes.
column7: Two hands empty. One voice remains at the altar.

column5: She calls herself the Mother. Ask the empty houses what she raised here. End her watch at the altar and let the drowned village sleep.
column6: Kill the Hex Mother at the bog altar.
column7: The bells are only bells again. You have given this place a night of its own.

column5: The bell keepers always find their way back. Three fewer on the paths will buy the village another quiet evening.
column6: Kill 3 bog cultists for Oduya.
column7: That will do. Come back when the bells start again.

column5: Forty gold keeps the village lamps burning. I will not have the children cross those boards in the dark.
column6: Pay Oduya 40 gold for lamp oil.
column7: There. A light in every window that still has one.
